A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLMNodeBed study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, backbone comparisons, prediction-error analyses, and computational timings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds heterophilic-graph comparisons, ogbn-products evaluation, GLEM results, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The existing encoding, TAPE, predictor, and zero-shot prompting procedures remain unchanged. Renaming LLM-as-Reasoner to LLM-as-Explainer does not change its operation. GLEM and H2GCN expand the evaluated comparisons rather than revise the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original ten datasets and evaluates Cornell, Texas, Wisconsin, and Washington, introducing strongly heterophilic webpage-classification coverage. Appendix D additionally evaluates ogbn-products, with 2,449,029 nodes and 47 product categories, substantially extending graph-scale coverage.

E2.justification: GLEM is added to the main accuracy and Macro-F1 comparisons, H2GCN to encoder comparisons, and GAT with LLM embeddings to the large-graph evaluation. Existing LLM comparators remain. DeepSeek-Chat becomes DeepSeek-V3 with identical scores; an actual backend change is not established.

E3.justification: Existing evaluation settings largely remain. Added experiments specify heterophilic train/validation/test splits of 10/10/80 and 60/20/20, and an ogbn-products protocol using Qwen2.5-3B embeddings and a reduced 221,309-node test set. Memory measurement during training and inference is added for Cora, WikiCS, and arXiv.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 now directly tests the encoder-benefit hypothesis on four strongly heterophilic graphs, including comparisons with H2GCN. Section 4.3 adds memory analysis, while the full semi-supervised training-time analysis is removed. Existing backbone-sensitivity, biased-prediction, and hallucination analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The four-run statement, existing ± reporting, and single-run exception for LLMIT on arXiv are retained. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures appear. The new large-graph and memory tables provide point estimates.

E6.justification: Matched scores remain unchanged, but new GLEM results alter some rankings: semi-supervised Pubmed accuracy is 81.70%, above the previous winner LLMIT at 80.99%. v2 adds heterophilic, ogbn-products, and memory results and deletes v1 Table 17's timings. Its new Texas claim overstates GCN's gain: Table 5 shows 58.67 versus 55.20, a 3.47-point difference, rather than the stated 12%.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, mutual-information decomposition in Equation (1), and mathematical descriptions of TAPE and LLaGA are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion expand the stated benchmark contribution from ten to fourteen datasets and from over 2,200 to over 2,700 models, explicitly listing eight classic baselines. The principal comparative conclusions remain; the encoder takeaway is refined to less informative graphs, including heterophilic ones.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes the original lower-homophily datasets from the newly evaluated strongly heterophilic graphs, refining its interpretation of encoder benefits. It adds memory-based deployment guidance and explains resource-driven exclusions from large-graph evaluation. Existing mechanism explanations and predictor-failure interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds H2GCN search ranges, GLEM EM/LoRA settings, heterophilic-data preparation, and a direct processed-data repository reference. Appendix D specifies large-graph features and resource constraints. Most existing implementation details remain, but the complete semi-supervised training-time breakdown is removed.

R1.justification: New citations include H2GCN, the heterophilic-data source, GRENADE, and GAugLLM. WebWalker is removed, and model-report references change to Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek-V3. The taxonomy and positioning relative to GLBench remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, consistently replaces Reasoner with Explainer, revises selected explanatory paragraphs, rewrites the impact statement, and adds acknowledgments and a large-graph appendix. The main section sequence and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated heterophily, large-graph, and memory tables; moves and expands the dataset-statistics table into the main text; and inserts GLEM rows into comparison tables. Figure 1 gains dataset and evaluation bands. The semi-supervised timing table is removed, while most other figures retain their appearance.

improvement.justification: The four strongly heterophilic datasets and H2GCN comparisons address an important weakness: v1 supported its heterophily conclusion using graphs with homophily above 55%. GLEM comparisons, million-node evaluation, and memory measurements further strengthen the benchmark's evidential and practical value. These gains outweigh the loss of the semi-supervised timing table and the new overstatement of GCN's Texas improvement.
